Proposed model linking Capns1 to cholesterol metabolism in ethanol‐treated liver

Proposed model linking Capns1 to cholesterol metabolism in ethanol‐treated liver. Schematic illustration summarizing the proposed role of Capns1‐dependent calpain activity in regulating hepatic cholesterol metabolism during ethanol exposure. Ethanol feeding is associated with dysregulated calpain signaling, altered LXRα subcellular localization, and activation of cholesterol biosynthetic pathways. Capns1 knockdown suppresses ethanol‐induced cholesterol biosynthesis, promotes LXRα nuclear translocation, and increases the cleaved/pro‐HMGCR ratio, thereby limiting functional HMGCR availability. Green arrows indicate regulatory relationships between Calpain and downstream targets. Question marks (?) denote connections that are proposed based on the collective data but for which the direct molecular mechanisms remain to be established. Collectively, these changes contribute to improved cholesterol homeostasis and are associated with reduced hepatic cholesterol accumulation in ethanol‐treated mice
